$comment: POST /v1.0/subscriptions, request and response subscription, 201. Read from the Graph v1.0 reference, checked 2026-09-15. The action a subscription trigger's `create` names: the HOST calls it with its own URL, an absolute expiry it computed, and the connection's clientState, and reads the lease from the response's `expirationDateTime` (ISO 8601 with a seven-digit fraction). Before Graph answers, it POSTs `?validationToken=...` to the notification URL and expects the token back as text/plain within 10 seconds -- the trigger's handshake.
title: Outlook subscription
description: Subscribe to change notifications on the connected account's calendar events. The host's subscription machinery calls this; it is not a node most workflows need.
$idempotencyComment: Graph refuses a duplicate -- "When a subscription request contains the same values for changeType and resource that an existing subscription contains, the request fails with an HTTP error code 409 Conflict" -- so a retry cannot open a second subscription on the same resource. But a retry after a TIMEOUT cannot tell whether the first one was created, and a 409 on the retry does not carry its id, so the host must list subscriptions to recover. Honestly unsafe-to-replay.

config.label: Changes
config.description: Which changes raise a notification. Graph accepts a comma-separated combination.

config.label: Resource
config.description: The Graph resource to watch, without the base URL. `me/events` is the connected account's calendar events.

config.label: Notification URL
config.description: The HTTPS URL the host mounts for this trigger. Graph validates it with a validationToken challenge before creating the subscription, then POSTs change notifications to it.

config.label: Lifecycle notification URL
config.description: Where Graph sends `reauthorizationRequired`, `subscriptionRemoved` and `missed` events. May be the notification URL itself. Optional, but without it a subscription Graph removed is one nobody hears about.

config.label: Expires at
config.description: When the subscription expires, as an ISO 8601 instant in UTC. The host computes now + the trigger's lifetime; Graph caps an event subscription at 10080 minutes (under seven days) and raises anything under 45 minutes to 45.
config.$comment: The HOST supplies the absolute instant, so the package stays clockless -- a faker that read the clock could not be reproduced byte for byte across three runtimes.

config.label: Client state
config.description: The connection's clientState. The host fills this from the connection -- never type a value here. Graph echoes it inside every notification, and that echo is how a delivery is verified. At most 128 characters.
config.$comment: A CREDENTIAL sent in the body -- the same shape as Google's channel token, which is what makes `request.fromCredentials` vocabulary rather than a special case. Until it exists the host passes the value as config. Recorded in .ai/plans/vocabulary-deferred.md.

outputShape.description: The subscription id. subscription_renew and subscription_delete need it.
When it expires, ISO 8601 UTC with a seven-digit fraction. The subscription trigger's lease is built from this.
Which estate this ran against: fake, sandbox or live.
